objective: Determine, before any wave case is authorised, whether the installed wave boundary conditions announce at run time which of the nine wave theories they actually constructed, because a wave capability that cannot print what it selected can be exercised but cannot be proven, and this lab's most-cited lesson is that configured is not active
rationale: The dead-lever audit produced one instance of the failure mode at capability scale rather than at knob scale: zero tracked files in this repository reference any wave machinery at all, against 1,825 mentioning the interface field by the identical pipeline. The wave library is present with nine theories, the two wave patch fields and active absorption; it is shipped, it is linked into three solvers, and it has never once been run here. A capability step to run it is already filed at 135 core minutes. This item is the zero-compute question underneath that purchase and it is deliberately NOT a duplicate of it: that item asks whether a wave can be generated and absorbed, this one asks whether the answer would be PROVABLE when it arrives. The lab has the measured precedent that makes the question worth asking rather than assuming. An adjoint reordering lever was requested in 257 archived runs and has a readback in zero of them, so no conclusion drawn under it can be defended; and a preconditioner banner in the same toolchain was measured printing overlap and fill-level settings for a preconditioner that was not the one built, with the linear solver's own readback contradicting the banner in the same file. Both were found AFTER the runs. THE NULL, AND IT IS NOT FITTED: the current state of the shipped binary and its sources, which nobody in this lab wrote and which was not built with this question in mind. There is no first step here that could be tuned. THE IDENTITY TEST, owner rule W dash 2: the gated quantity is whether a named string identifying the selected wave theory reaches a run's standard output or its solver log. Could that be derived by construction from its own inputs? It could be faked by one specific route and that route is excluded in advance: reading the theory name back out of the case dictionary that SET it proves only that a text file can be read twice, which is precisely the shipped-helper blindness this lab has already caught itself in. The evidence admitted is therefore an emission from the running process or from the compiled library's own symbol and string tables, and NOT the input dictionary.
gate: ZERO COMPUTE and no solve. Three-valued and declared before looking. PROVABLE if the wave patch field's construction path in the installed sources or its compiled strings carries an emission naming the selected theory, and the emission is reachable at the verbosity a normal run uses; the naval capability purchase then proceeds unchanged and this item closes cheap. UNPROVABLE if no such emission exists, in which case the 135 core-minute purchase must first buy a launcher-side echo of the wave properties dictionary at run start -- the mechanism this lab has already proven works, having read a solver setting out of a compressed archived log with the echoed dictionary's hash matching the archived dictionary -- or else it must ship with the blind spot stated on the face of its result. NO VERDICT if the installed sources are not readable here, which is a finding about this install and is reported as one. POSITIVE AND NEGATIVE CONTROLS ARE MANDATORY AND ARE REPORTED FIRST, because the whole answer is a search that may return nothing and a search returning nothing is indistinguishable from a search that was never pointed anywhere: the positive control is any solver setting in the same install that IS known to echo, and the negative control is a string that certainly does not exist. A search that cannot find the positive control does not get to report the negative.
cost_basis: ZERO solver compute; the work is reading an installed library's sources and symbol tables on this host. Scored in agent tool calls. Forecast 12 calls, above this lab's bounded-question band of 2 to 5 because the controls are mandatory and each is a call, and well below the build-and-verify band of 33 to 72 because nothing is built. Actual counted from the executing agent's transcript. The purchase this protects is 135 core minutes, so the ratio of what it costs to what it could redirect is the argument for running it first.
expected_knowledge_gain: THE DISCRIMINATING OUTCOME. Belief moves in the unprovable branch and moves a purchase with it: the naval capability step would then be known in advance to produce a capability claim with no activity proof behind it, which is the same shape as the 257 unproven reordering requests but caught before the spend instead of years after, and the purchase gets an echo attached to it for a few tool calls rather than being re-run later. Belief also moves in the provable branch, though less: it converts an assumption every naval estimate on the board currently inherits into a checked fact. The genuinely uninformative outcome is a search that finds nothing while the positive control also finds nothing, and the gate refuses to report that as a negative.
hard_criterion_note: Starts no flow case. It reads an installed library and reports whether a future run could be proven, which is an instrument question about this host rather than a physics question.
